cells.tense: You are at the point of deciding, and you have the pen in hand now.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: When a pull comes at the direction you picked, hold the line one more day than you want to. Nothing louder than that.
cells.core:
A connection is being chosen here, and your practice is where it lands. You bring an old way of moving and someone else brings theirs, and you have already tried a few steps together. In the space where you refine things, the two ways are finding one line, and it holds. What you built by repetition is what lets the two of you move as one without losing either.

The direction you picked will get a shove from somewhere. Hold it one more day than you want to. That is all. You will have what a defended choice feels like in the body, and the practice you built will have a heading instead of a drift. If the shove turns out to be right, you will know that by holding, not by folding early.
cells.sheetLine: A chosen direction, kept for one more day.
cells.verb: Choosing one connection and letting two ways of moving become a single line
cells.place: A practice room, kept by attention, where skill is built by repetition

cells.tense: You are bracing for a merge that hasn't happened yet, and you cannot write it in advance.
cells.act: let the abundance be seen and used
cells.ask: Pick what you and another person already built and use it as finished. Let it stand where it is, nothing added.
cells.core:
There is a pull to get the two of you to one flow faster than it can go. You rehearse the joining, you test it, you keep the practice lit bright to make it arrive. A merge that is being forced stops being a choice and becomes a project. The other person can feel the rehearsal on them, and the room gets smaller each time you check whether you have become one yet.

A finishing already happened that you are not counting. Take what you and someone else made and use it as it stands, without improving it first. That is not giving up on the practice; it is letting the two of you enjoy what you already are, which is what makes the next step a step instead of a rescue.
cells.sheetLine: The merge is being rehearsed instead of lived.
cells.verb: Choosing one connection and letting two ways of moving become a single line

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that has already closed behind you.
cells.act: list the pulls on you and mark which are yours
cells.ask: Name the pulls on you lately, then mark which began with you and which arrived from elsewhere. You don't have to act on any of it.
cells.core:
A connection was chosen and the practice has gone on without you fully in it. You do the moves — the repetitions, the refinements — the way you learned them from someone else's direction, and the two-way flow is running one way. What was decided back there is still steering the room, and you are standing just outside it, keeping the light on for a merge that already happened or already didn't.

Before you do anything about that, know what is pulling at you. Set the pulls out where you can see them, then mark which started with you and which came in from elsewhere. You do not have to act on the list. Seeing which pressure is genuinely yours is what puts the pen back in your hand; the practice comes after that, not before.
cells.sheetLine: The doors these steps came through are behind you.
cells.verb: Choosing one connection and letting two ways of moving become a single line
cells.place: A practice room, kept by attention, where skill is built by repetition

cells.tense: You are already writing in the room, but the pen is not in your hand.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: When someone is stuck on what you have already worked through, point to the way you went. Once, plainly, then let it be.
cells.core:
There is a passage being found in this practice, and you would call it the method, the routine, the way this room works. You show up and the steps happen. Asked how you found the way through, you would say you followed what was already laid down. Some of that route you cleared yourself. The practice is more yours than the account of it admits, and the two of you keep moving through a door someone is quietly holding open.

You know a passage out of something because you came through it. Point someone to that route, once, and say what you did to find it. Then let them walk it. That is the whole act — the pen returning to the hand that was already writing.
cells.sheetLine: The route through is one you built.
cells.verb: Choosing one connection and letting two ways of moving become a single line

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person is deliberately guarding openness and keeping things from merging; the record shows a connection being chosen, not a strategy. A reader could rightly say the two streams were never theirs to choose, so the refusal is not a doing. The asks each survive a wrong read: carrying one line, naming what's finished, keeping one page, pointing once cost nothing even if the diagnosis is off. The sentence that serves me more than them is the balanced core's 'the refusal is still a choice'; it flatters the reading, so it is cut.
